So he went back to him, and Khosrau became angry and did not answer him, and he sent a messenger to the people of Persia: I have removed Shahrazad from you and appointed Farkhan over you. Then he gave the messenger a small, delicate piece of paper, and said: If Farkhan takes over the kingdom and his brother submits to him, give him this. So when Shahrazad read the letter He said: Hearing and obedience, and he got down from his bed and Farkhan sat down and gave him the paper and said: Bring me Shahrazad and brought him forward to behead him, he said: Do not hurry until I write my will, he said: Yes, so he called for the basket and gave him the papers, he said: All this I consulted with Khosrow about you and you wanted to kill me with one letter, so he returned the kingdom to his brother Shahrazad, and Shahrazad wrote to Caesar, King of al-Rum 30:I have a need from you that neither the cold nor the papers can bear, so meet me and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, for I will meet you with fifty Persians, so Caesar came with five hundred thousand Romans, and he began to place spies before him on the road, and he was afraid that he had deceived him until his spies told him that he had only fifty men with him, then he spread out for them and they met in a brocade tent that had been made for them, with each of them having a knife, so they called an interpreter between them, and Shahrazad said: Those who destroyed your cities are my brother and I with our treachery and our bravery, and Khosrow envied us He wanted to kill my brother, but I refused. Then he ordered my brother to kill me, and we have all deposed him. We will fight him with you. He said, You have both done well. Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two people, and if it goes beyond two people, it is revealed. He said, Yes. So they both killed the translators with their knives, and God destroyed Khosrau. The report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and he and the Muslims rejoiced. This is a strange context and a wondrous construction. Let us talk about the words of these noble verses. The Almighty said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” We have already discussed the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. As for the Romans, they are from the lineage of Esau, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. They are cousins of the Children of Israel, and they are called the sons of the yellow ones. They were of the Greek religion. The Greeks are from the lineage of Japheth, son of Noah, cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven planets, called the Mutahira, and they prayed to the North Pole. They founded Damascus and built its temple, which had niches facing the north. The Romans followed their religion until about three hundred years after the mission of Christ. Among the kings of the Levant and the island was one called Caesar. The first of the kings to enter the Christian religion was Constantine, son of Qustus, and his mother was Mary, the Hellenic, the Fedqani from the land of Harran. She had converted to Christianity before him, so she invited him to her religion. Before that, he was a philosopher, so he followed her, it is said, out of fear. The Christians met with him and debated in his time with Abdullah bin Arius, and they differed in a widespread and scattered disagreement that was not regulated, except that three hundred and eighteen bishops from their group agreed, so they established for Constantine the doctrine, which they call the great trust, but it is in fact the contemptible betrayal, and they established for him laws, meaning books of rulings of prohibition and permission, and other things that they needed, and they changed the religion of Christ, peace be upon him, and they added to it and subtracted from it, so they prayed to the east, and replaced the Sabbath with Sunday, and they worshipped the cross and made the pig permissible, and they took holidays that they created like the Feast of the Cross, the Mass, the Epiphany, and other motives and snakes, and they made for him the door, and he is their chief, then the patriarchs, then the metropolitans, then the bishops and presbyters, then the deacons, and they invented monasticism, and the king built for them churches and temples, and he founded the city attributed to him, which is Constantinople. It is said that he built twelve thousand churches in his days, and he built Bethlehem with three altars, and his mother built the garbage, and these are the royalists, meaning those who are On the king's religion. Then came after them the Jacobites, the followers of Jacob the Cobbler, then the Nestorians, the followers of Nestorius, and they are many groups and sects, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They split into seventy-two sects. The point is that they continued in Christianity, whenever Caesar died, another succeeded him until the last of them was Heraclius, and he was one of the wisest men, and one of the most prudent and clever of kings, and the most profound of them in depth, and the most far-reaching of them in opinion, so he ruled over them with great leadership and great splendor, so Khosrau, the king of Persia, opposed him and ruled the countries such as Iraq, Khorasan, Rayy and all the lands of the Persians, and he is Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf, and his kingdom was larger than Caesar’s kingdom, and he had the leadership of the Persians, and the foolishness of the Persians, and they were Zoroastrians who worshipped fire, so it was mentioned from Ikrimah that: He sent his deputies and his army to him and they fought him, and it is well-known that Khosrau himself invaded his country, so he defeated him, crushed him and confined him, until nothing remained with him except the city of Constantinople. He besieged him there for a long time, until it became too narrow for him, and the Christians held him in excessive esteem. Khosrow was not able to conquer the country, nor was he able to do so because of its fortifications, as half of it was on the land side, and the other half was on the sea side, so the provisions and supplies came to them from there. When the matter dragged on, Caesar plotted, and saw in himself a deception, so he asked Khosrow to leave his country in exchange for money that he would reconcile with him and stipulate whatever he wanted. He agreed to that, and asked him for huge sums of money that no king of the world could afford, such as gold, jewels, fabrics, slave girls, servants, and many other things. Caesar obeyed him and made him believe that he had everything he asked for, and his mind was independent when he asked him what he asked for. If he and he had gathered together, their ability would be incapable of collecting a tenth of it. Khosrow asked that he be able to go to the Levant and the regions of his kingdom, to strive to obtain that from his treasures, his earnings, and his treasures, so he released him. When Caesar decided to leave the city of Constantinople, he gathered the people of He said: I am going out on a matter that I have decided with a group that I have appointed from my army. If I return to you before a year, then I am your king. If I do not return to you before that, then you have the choice: if you wish, you may continue to pledge allegiance to me, or if you wish, you may appoint someone other than me over you. They replied: You are our king as long as I live, even if I am absent for ten years. When he left Constantinople, he went out with a group of soldiers of this size, and Khosrow was camped at Constantinople, waiting for him to return. Caesar immediately mounted and marched quickly until he reached Persia. He ravaged their country, killing its men and its fighters, one by one. He continued killing until he reached Al-Mada’in, which was the seat of Khosrow’s kingdom. He killed everyone there and took all their provisions and money, and took his women and harem captive. He shaved his son’s head and put him on his donkey. He sent with him bracelets from his people in the utmost humiliation and disgrace. He wrote to Khosrow saying: This is what you asked for, take it. When Khosrow heard of that, he took him from He said: “The grief is that which only God Almighty can count, and his anger at the country intensified, so he intensified his siege of it with every possible means, but he was unable to do that. When he was unable to do that, he rode to take the road from the ford of the Gihon, which was the only way for Caesar to reach Constantinople. When Caesar learned of that, he devised a great trick that had never been done before, which was that he stationed his soldiers and the crops that he had with him at the mouth of the ford, and rode with some of the army, and ordered loads of straw, dung, and manure to be carried with him, and he walked for about a day, ascending in the water, then he ordered those loads to be thrown into the river. When they passed by Khosrau, he and his soldiers thought that they had waded from there, so they rode in pursuit of them, and the ford was empty of the Persians. Caesar came forward and ordered them to rise and wade, so they waded and hastened their march, and they missed Khosrau and his soldiers, and entered Constantinople. That was a day witnessed by the Christians, and Khosrau and his armies remained confused, not knowing what to do. They did not obtain Caesar’s country, and their country had been destroyed by the Romans, and their crops were taken, and their children and women were taken captive. This was due to the Romans’ victory over Persia, and that was nine years after the Persians had defeated the Romans. The battle that took place between Persia and the Romans when the Romans were victorious was between Adhraat and Busra, as mentioned by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. It is the edge of the Levant, next to the Hijaz. Mujahid said: This was in Al-Jazira, and it is the closest land of the Romans to Persia. And God knows best. Then the Romans defeated the Persians after a few years, which were nine, because “bad’a” in the speech of the Arabs means between three and nine. This is also what came in the hadith narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and others on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Jumahi on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Bakr while lamenting the verse “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated” Have you not taken precautions, O Abu Bakr? Because “bad’a means between three and nine?” Then he said: This is a good and strange hadith from this chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he said the same. God the Almighty says: To God belongs the command before and after meaning before that and after it. It was built on the damma because it separated the noun from the complement, which is His saying before from the complement. I intended And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God's victory meaning the Romans, the followers of Caesar, the king of Syria, over the Persians, the followers of Kisra, who were the Magians. The victory of the Romans over the Persians on the day of the Battle of Badr was stated by many scholars, such as Ibn Abbas, Al-Thawri, Al-Suddi and others. It was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bazzar on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Atiyyah on the authority of Abu Sa'id who said: When the day of Badr came, the Romans were victorious over the Persians, so the believers were amazed by it and rejoiced over it, and God the Almighty revealed: "And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God's victory. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful." Others said: Rather, the victory of the Romans over the Persians was in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. This was said by Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others. Some of them based this statement on the fact that Caesar had vowed that if God granted him victory over Khosrau, he would walk from Homs to Aelia, which is Jerusalem, as thanks to God Almighty, and he did so. But when he reached Jerusalem, he did not leave until he received the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), which he had sent with Dihya bin Khalifah. Dihya gave it to the ruler of Busra, who then handed it over to Caesar. When it reached Caesar, he asked who was in Ash-Sham from the Arabs of Hijaz. Abu Sufyan brought him Sakhr bin Harb Al-Umawi with a group of the leaders of Quraysh who were in Gaza. They were brought to him and sat before him. He said: Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet? Abu Sufyan said: I will. He said to his companions and seated them behind him: I will ask this man about this man, and if he lies, then call him a liar. Abu Sufyan said: By God, were it not for the fact that they would attribute lies to me, I would have lied. Heraclius asked him about his lineage and description. Among the things he asked was: Will he betray? I said: No, and we are in a period of time with him in which we do not know what he will do. He meant by that the truce that had been signed between the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the infidels of Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyyah to stop the war between them for ten years. They used this as evidence that the victory of the Romans over the Persians was in the year of Hudaybiyyah, because Caesar only fulfilled his vow after Hudaybiyyah, and God knows best. Those who hold the first view can respond to this by saying that his country had been destroyed and scattered, so he was not able to fulfill his vow until he had repaired what was necessary and inspected his country. Then, after four years of his victory, he fulfilled his vow, and God knows best. The matter in this regard is easy and straightforward, except that when Persia defeated the Romans, the believers were upset. When the Romans defeated the Persians, the believers rejoiced because the Romans were People of the Book, and so they were closer to the believers than the Magians, as God the Almighty said: “You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God. And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” And God the Almighty said here: “And on that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Asid Al-Kalabi told me: I heard Al-Ala’ bin Al-Zubayr Al-Kalabi narrating on the authority of his father, who said: I saw the Persians defeat the Romans, then I saw the Romans defeat the Persians, then I saw the Muslims defeat the Persians and the Romans, all of that in fifteen years. And the Almighty’s saying: And He is the Exalted in Might meaning in His victory and vengeance against His enemies, the Most Merciful to His believing servants. And the Almighty’s saying: The promise of God - God never breaks His promise meaning that what We have informed you of, O Muhammad, that We will give victory to the Romans over the Persians is a true promise from God, and a true report that will never break its promise. It must happen and come to pass, because it is God’s law that He gives victory to the one of the two warring factions that is closest to the truth, and that He will grant it the best outcome. But most people do not know meaning about God’s rule in His universe and His well-thought-out actions that are in accordance with justice. God the Almighty says: {They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.} Meaning, most people have no knowledge except of this world, its earnings, its affairs and everything in it. They are clever and intelligent in acquiring it and how to earn it, but they are heedless of what will benefit them in the Hereafter, as if one of them is an idiot with no mind or thought. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: By God, one of them would reach such a level of his worldly life that he would turn a dirham over on his fingernail and tell you its weight and how best to pray. Ibn Abbas said about God the Almighty’s saying: {They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.} Meaning, the disbelievers know the worldly affairs, but they are ignorant of religious matters.
30:7: These verses were revealed when Shapur, the Persian king, conquered the Levant, the Arabian Peninsula, and the far reaches of Byzantine territory. Heraclius, the Byzantine king, was forced to flee to Constantinople and besiege him there for a long time. Then the empire returned to Heraclius, as will be mentioned later. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God Almighty: {Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated * In the lowest land}. He said: defeated and defeated. He said: The polytheists loved for Persia to prevail over the Romans, because they were idolaters, and the Muslims loved for the Romans to prevail over the Persians, because they were People of the Book. This was mentioned to Abu Bakr, who mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They will be defeated. Abu Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: Set a time limit between us and you. If we are victorious, then such and such will be for us, and if you are victorious, then such and such will be for you. So he set a time limit of five years, but they did not prevail. So Abu Bakr mentioned this to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Why did you not make it less than - I think he said ten? Saeed bin Jubair said: A few is less than ten, then the Romans appeared after that. He said: This is what His words: {Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated * In the lowest land, and they are after that. They will be victorious. Within three to nine years. To God belongs the command before and after. And that Day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory. He gives victory to whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. This is how it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i, both on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Harith, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Amr, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id al-Thawri, with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan ghareeb. We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sagani, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Amr, with this chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated it: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa’id or Sa’id al-Tha’labi, who is called Abu Sa’d, from the people of Tarsus, narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us, and he mentioned it. And according to them, Sufyan said: I was informed that they were victorious on the day of Badr. Another Hadith Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A’mash narrated from Muslim from Masruq who said: Abdullah said: Five have passed: Ad-Dukhan, Ad-Lazzam, Ad-Batsha, Al-Qamar, and Ar-Rum. Both of them narrated it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, Al-Maharibi narrated to us from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Amir - he is Al-Sha’bi - from Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him who said: Persia was victorious over the Romans, and the polytheists loved for Persia to be victorious over the Romans. The Muslims loved for the Romans to be victorious over the Persians because they are the People of the Book and they are closer to their religion. So when the verse “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years” was revealed, they said: O Abu Bakr, your companion says that the Romans will be victorious over the Persians within three to nine years. He said: He is speaking the truth. They said: Would you like us to gamble with you? So they pledged allegiance to him for four she-camels for seven years. The seven days passed and nothing happened, so the polytheists rejoiced at that, and it was difficult for the Muslims. So this was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, What do you mean by a few years? They said, Less than ten. He said, Go and give them more, and add two years to the term. So the two years had not passed when the caravans brought report of the Romans’ victory over the Persians, and the believers rejoiced at that.” And God, the Most High, revealed: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated. In the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice. In God’s victory. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. [This is] the promise of God; God does not fail in His promise.” Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Omar Al-Wakii told us, Mumin told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: When the verse, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome,” was revealed, the polytheists said to Abu Bakr, Don’t you see what your companion is saying? He claims that the Romans will defeat the Persians. He said, My companion has spoken the truth. They said, Would you like us to take a risk? So he set a deadline between him and them, and the deadline was due before the Romans defeated the Persians. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was upset and disliked it, and he said to Abu Bakr, What made you do this? He said, To confirm what God and His Messenger have said. He said, Expose yourself to them and make the risk great, and make it last for a few years. Abu Bakr came to them and said to them, Would you like to return, for returning is better? They said, Yes. Those years had not passed until the Romans defeated the Persians, and they tied up their horses in Al-Madain and built the Roman city. Abu Bakr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: This is ill-gotten gain. He said: Give it in charity. Another hadith Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail bin Abi Uways told us, Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr on the authority of Niyar bin Mukram Al-Aslami, who said: When the verse, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land. But after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years,” was revealed, the Persians were the ones who had conquered the Romans on the day this verse was revealed, and the Muslims loved the Romans’ victory over them, because they and they were People of the Book. Concerning that, God says: “And on that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.” The Quraysh loved the Persians’ victory, because they and they were not People of the Book, nor did they believe in the Resurrection. So when God revealed this verse, Abu Bakr went out shouting in the outskirts of Mecca, “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land. But after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years.” Some of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr: That is between us and you. Your companion claimed that the Romans would overcome the Persians in three to nine years. Doesn’t he…” Shall we bet you on that? He said: Yes, and that was before betting was forbidden. So Abu Bakr and the polytheists made a bet and agreed upon the bet and said to Abu Bakr: How much do you make a few years? From three to nine years, name a middle ground between us and you. So they named six years between them. So the six years passed before they were victorious, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr’s pledge. When the seventh year began, the Romans defeated the Persians. The Muslims criticized Abu Bakr for naming six years. He said: Because God said in a few years. He said: At that time, many people embraced Islam. This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it. Then he said: This is a good and authentic hadith. We do not know it except from the hadith of Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad. Something similar to this was narrated in a mursal form on the authority of a group of the Tabi’un, such as Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Al-Zuhri, and others. One of the strangest of these chains of transmission is what Imam Sunayd ibn Dawud narrated in his Tafsir, where he said: Hajjaj told me on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah on the authority of Ikrimah who said: There was a woman in Persia who only gave birth to heroic kings. Khosrow summoned her and said: I want to send an army to the Romans and appoint over them a man from your sons, so advise me which of them should I appoint?! She said: This is so-and-so, and he is more cunning than a fox and more cautious than a falcon. This is Farkhan, and he is sharper than a spear. This is Shahrazad, and he is more patient than so-and-so, meaning her three sons. Appoint whichever of them you wish. He said: I have appointed the patient one. So he appointed Shahrazad, and he marched to the Romans with the people of Persia, defeated them, destroyed their cities, and cut down their olive trees. Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah said: I narrated this hadith to Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and he said: Have you not seen the land of Ash-Sham? I said: No. He said: If you had seen it, you would have seen the cities that were destroyed and the olive trees that were cut down. Then I came to Syria after that and saw it. Ata Al-Khurasani said: Yahya bin Ya`mar told me that Caesar sent a man called Qutmah with an army of Romans, and Khosrow sent Shahrazad. They met at Adhraat and Busra, which is the closest part of Syria to you. The Persians met the Romans and defeated them. The infidels of Quraysh rejoiced at that, but the Muslims hated it. `Ikrimah said: The polytheists met the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are illiterate. Your brothers from the Persians have defeated our brothers from the People of the Book, and if you fight us, we will defeat you. Then God revealed: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to nine years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in God’s victory. He gives victory to whom He wills.” Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq went out to the infidels and said: “Have you rejoiced at the victory of your brothers over our brothers? Do not rejoice, and do not let God comfort your eyes. By God, God will make the Romans victorious over the Persians.” He told us about that. Our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Abi bin Khalaf stood up and said: You have lied, O Abu Fadil. Abu Bakr said to him: You are a liar, O enemy of God. He said: I will give you ten she-camels from me and ten she-camels from you. If the Romans defeat the Persians, you will be fined, and if the Persians defeat them, you will be fined for three years. Then Abu Bakr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He said: This is not what you said. The term ‘female camel’ is between three and nine. So he increased the risk and extended the term. Abu Bakr went out and met Abi, and said: Perhaps you regretted it? He said: No, come, I will increase the danger and give you an extension in the term, so make it one hundred camels for one hundred camels for nine years. He said: I have done so, and the Romans had defeated the Persians before that, and the Muslims defeated them. Ikrimah said: When the Persians defeated the Romans, Farkhan, the brother of Shahrazad, sat drinking, and said to his companions: I saw as if I was sitting on the throne of Khosrau. Khosrau heard about it, so Khosrau wrote to Shahrazad: When my letter reaches you, send me Farkhan’s head. So he wrote to him: O king, you will not find anyone like Farkhan who has the power to defeat and a voice against the enemy, so do not do that. So he wrote to him: There are men from Persia who succeed him, so hurry to me with his head. So he went back to him, and Khosrau became angry and did not answer him, and he sent a messenger to the people of Persia: I have removed Shahrazad from you and appointed Farkhan over you. Then he gave the messenger a small, delicate piece of paper, and said: If Farkhan takes over the kingdom and his brother submits to him, give him this. So when Shahrazad read the letter He said: Hearing and obedience, and he got down from his bed and Farkhan sat down and gave him the paper and said: Bring me Shahrazad and brought him forward to behead him, he said: Do not hurry until I write my will, he said: Yes, so he called for the basket and gave him the papers, he said: All this I consulted with Khosrow about you and you wanted to kill me with one letter, so he returned the kingdom to his brother Shahrazad, and Shahrazad wrote to Caesar, King of al-Rum 30:I have a need from you that neither the cold nor the papers can bear, so meet me and do not meet me except with fifty Romans, for I will meet you with fifty Persians, so Caesar came with five hundred thousand Romans, and he began to place spies before him on the road, and he was afraid that he had deceived him until his spies told him that he had only fifty men with him, then he spread out for them and they met in a brocade tent that had been made for them, with each of them having a knife, so they called an interpreter between them, and Shahrazad said: Those who destroyed your cities are my brother and I with our treachery and our bravery, and Khosrow envied us He wanted to kill my brother, but I refused. Then he ordered my brother to kill me, and we have all deposed him. We will fight him with you. He said, You have both done well. Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two people, and if it goes beyond two people, it is revealed. He said, Yes. So they both killed the translators with their knives, and God destroyed Khosrau. The report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and he and the Muslims rejoiced. This is a strange context and a wondrous construction. Let us talk about the words of these noble verses. The Almighty said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated.” We have already discussed the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. As for the Romans, they are from the lineage of Esau, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. They are cousins of the Children of Israel, and they are called the sons of the yellow ones. They were of the Greek religion. The Greeks are from the lineage of Japheth, son of Noah, cousins of the Turks. They used to worship the seven planets, called the Mutahira, and they prayed to the North Pole. They founded Damascus and built its temple, which had niches facing the north. The Romans followed their religion until about three hundred years after the mission of Christ. Among the kings of the Levant and the island was one called Caesar. The first of the kings to enter the Christian religion was Constantine, son of Qustus, and his mother was Mary, the Hellenic, the Fedqani from the land of Harran. She had converted to Christianity before him, so she invited him to her religion. Before that, he was a philosopher, so he followed her, it is said, out of fear. The Christians met with him and debated in his time with Abdullah bin Arius, and they differed in a widespread and scattered disagreement that was not regulated, except that three hundred and eighteen bishops from their group agreed, so they established for Constantine the doctrine, which they call the great trust, but it is in fact the contemptible betrayal, and they established for him laws, meaning books of rulings of prohibition and permission, and other things that they needed, and they changed the religion of Christ, peace be upon him, and they added to it and subtracted from it, so they prayed to the east, and replaced the Sabbath with Sunday, and they worshipped the cross and made the pig permissible, and they took holidays that they created like the Feast of the Cross, the Mass, the Epiphany, and other motives and snakes, and they made for him the door, and he is their chief, then the patriarchs, then the metropolitans, then the bishops and presbyters, then the deacons, and they invented monasticism, and the king built for them churches and temples, and he founded the city attributed to him, which is Constantinople. It is said that he built twelve thousand churches in his days, and he built Bethlehem with three altars, and his mother built the garbage, and these are the royalists, meaning those who are On the king's religion. Then came after them the Jacobites, the followers of Jacob the Cobbler, then the Nestorians, the followers of Nestorius, and they are many groups and sects, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They split into seventy-two sects. The point is that they continued in Christianity, whenever Caesar died, another succeeded him until the last of them was Heraclius, and he was one of the wisest men, and one of the most prudent and clever of kings, and the most profound of them in depth, and the most far-reaching of them in opinion, so he ruled over them with great leadership and great splendor, so Khosrau, the king of Persia, opposed him and ruled the countries such as Iraq, Khorasan, Rayy and all the lands of the Persians, and he is Shapur Dhu al-Aktaf, and his kingdom was larger than Caesar’s kingdom, and he had the leadership of the Persians, and the foolishness of the Persians, and they were Zoroastrians who worshipped fire, so it was mentioned from Ikrimah that: He sent his deputies and his army to him and they fought him, and it is well-known that Khosrau himself invaded his country, so he defeated him, crushed him and confined him, until nothing remained with him except the city of Constantinople. He besieged him there for a long time, until it became too narrow for him, and the Christians held him in excessive esteem. Khosrow was not able to conquer the country, nor was he able to do so because of its fortifications, as half of it was on the land side, and the other half was on the sea side, so the provisions and supplies came to them from there. When the matter dragged on, Caesar plotted, and saw in himself a deception, so he asked Khosrow to leave his country in exchange for money that he would reconcile with him and stipulate whatever he wanted. He agreed to that, and asked him for huge sums of money that no king of the world could afford, such as gold, jewels, fabrics, slave girls, servants, and many other things. Caesar obeyed him and made him believe that he had everything he asked for, and his mind was independent when he asked him what he asked for. If he and he had gathered together, their ability would be incapable of collecting a tenth of it. Khosrow asked that he be able to go to the Levant and the regions of his kingdom, to strive to obtain that from his treasures, his earnings, and his treasures, so he released him. When Caesar decided to leave the city of Constantinople, he gathered the people of He said: I am going out on a matter that I have decided with a group that I have appointed from my army. If I return to you before a year, then I am your king. If I do not return to you before that, then you have the choice: if you wish, you may continue to pledge allegiance to me, or if you wish, you may appoint someone other than me over you. They replied: You are our king as long as I live, even if I am absent for ten years. When he left Constantinople, he went out with a group of soldiers of this size, and Khosrow was camped at Constantinople, waiting for him to return. Caesar immediately mounted and marched quickly until he reached Persia. He ravaged their country, killing its men and its fighters, one by one. He continued killing until he reached Al-Mada’in, which was the seat of Khosrow’s kingdom. He killed everyone there and took all their provisions and money, and took his women and harem captive. He shaved his son’s head and put him on his donkey. He sent with him bracelets from his people in the utmost humiliation and disgrace. He wrote to Khosrow saying: This is what you asked for, take it. When Khosrow heard of that, he took him from He said: “The grief is that which only God Almighty can count, and his anger at the country intensified, so he intensified his siege of it with every possible means, but he was unable to do that. When he was unable to do that, he rode to take the road from the ford of the Gihon, which was the only way for Caesar to reach Constantinople. When Caesar learned of that, he devised a great trick that had never been done before, which was that he stationed his soldiers and the crops that he had with him at the mouth of the ford, and rode with some of the army, and ordered loads of straw, dung, and manure to be carried with him, and he walked for about a day, ascending in the water, then he ordered those loads to be thrown into the river. When they passed by Khosrau, he and his soldiers thought that they had waded from there, so they rode in pursuit of them, and the ford was empty of the Persians. Caesar came forward and ordered them to rise and wade, so they waded and hastened their march, and they missed Khosrau and his soldiers, and entered Constantinople. That was a day witnessed by the Christians, and Khosrau and his armies remained confused, not knowing what to do. They did not obtain Caesar’s country, and their country had been destroyed by the Romans, and their crops were taken, and their children and women were taken captive. This was due to the Romans’ victory over Persia, and that was nine years after the Persians had defeated the Romans. The battle that took place between Persia and the Romans when the Romans were victorious was between Adhraat and Busra, as mentioned by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. It is the edge of the Levant, next to the Hijaz. Mujahid said: This was in Al-Jazira, and it is the closest land of the Romans to Persia. And God knows best. Then the Romans defeated the Persians after a few years, which were nine, because “bad’a” in the speech of the Arabs means between three and nine. This is also what came in the hadith narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and others on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Jumahi on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Bakr while lamenting the verse “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated” Have you not taken precautions, O Abu Bakr? Because “bad’a means between three and nine?” Then he said: This is a good and strange hadith from this chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he said the same. God the Almighty says: To God belongs the command before and after meaning before that and after it. It was built on the damma because it separated the noun from the complement, which is His saying before from the complement. I intended And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God's victory meaning the Romans, the followers of Caesar, the king of Syria, over the Persians, the followers of Kisra, who were the Magians. The victory of the Romans over the Persians on the day of the Battle of Badr was stated by many scholars, such as Ibn Abbas, Al-Thawri, Al-Suddi and others. It was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bazzar on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Atiyyah on the authority of Abu Sa'id who said: When the day of Badr came, the Romans were victorious over the Persians, so the believers were amazed by it and rejoiced over it, and God the Almighty revealed: "And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God's victory. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful." Others said: Rather, the victory of the Romans over the Persians was in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. This was said by Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others. Some of them based this statement on the fact that Caesar had vowed that if God granted him victory over Khosrau, he would walk from Homs to Aelia, which is Jerusalem, as thanks to God Almighty, and he did so. But when he reached Jerusalem, he did not leave until he received the letter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), which he had sent with Dihya bin Khalifah. Dihya gave it to the ruler of Busra, who then handed it over to Caesar. When it reached Caesar, he asked who was in Ash-Sham from the Arabs of Hijaz. Abu Sufyan brought him Sakhr bin Harb Al-Umawi with a group of the leaders of Quraysh who were in Gaza. They were brought to him and sat before him. He said: Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet? Abu Sufyan said: I will. He said to his companions and seated them behind him: I will ask this man about this man, and if he lies, then call him a liar. Abu Sufyan said: By God, were it not for the fact that they would attribute lies to me, I would have lied. Heraclius asked him about his lineage and description. Among the things he asked was: Will he betray? I said: No, and we are in a period of time with him in which we do not know what he will do. He meant by that the truce that had been signed between the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the infidels of Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyyah to stop the war between them for ten years. They used this as evidence that the victory of the Romans over the Persians was in the year of Hudaybiyyah, because Caesar only fulfilled his vow after Hudaybiyyah, and God knows best. Those who hold the first view can respond to this by saying that his country had been destroyed and scattered, so he was not able to fulfill his vow until he had repaired what was necessary and inspected his country. Then, after four years of his victory, he fulfilled his vow, and God knows best. The matter in this regard is easy and straightforward, except that when Persia defeated the Romans, the believers were upset. When the Romans defeated the Persians, the believers rejoiced because the Romans were People of the Book, and so they were closer to the believers than the Magians, as God the Almighty said: “You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God. And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” And God the Almighty said here: “And on that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Sufyan told us, Al-Walid told us, Asid Al-Kalabi told me: I heard Al-Ala’ bin Al-Zubayr Al-Kalabi narrating on the authority of his father, who said: I saw the Persians defeat the Romans, then I saw the Romans defeat the Persians, then I saw the Muslims defeat the Persians and the Romans, all of that in fifteen years. And the Almighty’s saying: And He is the Exalted in Might meaning in His victory and vengeance against His enemies, the Most Merciful to His believing servants. And the Almighty’s saying: The promise of God - God never breaks His promise meaning that what We have informed you of, O Muhammad, that We will give victory to the Romans over the Persians is a true promise from God, and a true report that will never break its promise. It must happen and come to pass, because it is God’s law that He gives victory to the one of the two warring factions that is closest to the truth, and that He will grant it the best outcome. But most people do not know meaning about God’s rule in His universe and His well-thought-out actions that are in accordance with justice. God the Almighty says: {They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.} Meaning, most people have no knowledge except of this world, its earnings, its affairs and everything in it. They are clever and intelligent in acquiring it and how to earn it, but they are heedless of what will benefit them in the Hereafter, as if one of them is an idiot with no mind or thought. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: By God, one of them would reach such a level of his worldly life that he would turn a dirham over on his fingernail and tell you its weight and how best to pray. Ibn Abbas said about God the Almighty’s saying: {They know only the outward appearance of the life of this world, while they are heedless of the Hereafter.} Meaning, the disbelievers know the worldly affairs, but they are ignorant of religious matters.
30:8: God Almighty says, alerting us to contemplate His creations, which indicate His existence and His uniqueness in creating them, and that there is no god but Him and no Lord but Him. He said, Have they not reflected within themselves? Meaning by this to look, ponder, and reflect on God’s creation of things from the upper and lower worlds and what is between them of various creatures and different kinds, so that they may know that they were not created in vain or falsely, but rather with truth, and that they are postponed to a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection. For this reason, God Almighty said, And indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord. Then He alerted them to the truth of His Messengers in what they brought from Him, with what supported them of miracles and clear evidence of the destruction of those who disbelieved in them and the salvation of those who believed them. God Almighty said, Have they not traveled through the land? Meaning with their understandings, minds, insight, and hearing the report of those who came before them. For this reason, He said, So they may see how was the end of those before them who were stronger than them in strength. Meaning, the past nations and previous generations were stronger than you, O you to whom Muhammad was sent, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they were granted peace and more wealth and children, and you were not given a tenth of what they were given, and they were empowered in this world with an empowerment you had not attained, and they lived long lives in it, so they lived it more than you, and exploited it more than you exploited it. And despite this, when their messengers came to them with clear proofs and they rejoiced in what they were given, God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from God, nor did their wealth or children stand between them and the punishment of God, nor did they repel from them an atom’s weight. And God would not wrong them in what He brought upon them of torment and punishment. But they were wronging themselves. That is, they were only given from themselves because they denied the signs of God and mocked them, and that was only because of their previous sins and their previous denial. For this reason, God Almighty said: Then the worst was the end of those who did evil, because they denied the signs of God and used to mock them. Just as God Almighty said: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they did not believe in Him the first time, and leave them in their transgression. They are blindly wandering. And God the Almighty said: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. And God the Almighty said: But if they turn away, then know that God only intends to afflict them with some of their sins. Based on this, as-sawā’ī is the accusative object of asa’awu. It was also said that the meaning of this is: Then the end of those who did evil was evil, meaning evil was their end because they denied the signs of God and used to mock them. Based on this, as-sawā’ī is the accusative predicate of kan. This is the interpretation of Ibn Jarir, and he transmitted it from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from them and from ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, and this is the apparent meaning - and God knows best - because of his statement: and used to mock them.

30:11: God the Almighty says: God begins creation and then repeats it meaning, just as He is able to begin it, He is also able to repeat it. Then to Him you will be returned meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, when every worker will be rewarded for his deeds. Then He says: And on the Day the Hour appears, the sinners will be despairing Ibn Abbas said: The sinners will despair. Mujahid said: The sinners will be disgraced. In another narration: The sinners will be depressed. And they will have no intercessors from among their partners meaning, the deities they used to worship besides God, and they disbelieved in them and betrayed them when they needed them most. Then God the Almighty says: And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will be divided Qatada said: By God, it is the division after which there will be no reunion. Meaning, when one is raised to the highest heavens and the other is lowered to the lowest of the low, that will be the final covenant between them. For this reason, God the Almighty says: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, rejoicing Mujahid and Qatadah said: They will be enjoying themselves. Yahya bin Abi Katheer said: He means listening to singing and music, and it is more general than all of this. Al-Ajjaj said: Praise be to God who gave the ink the right to follow. The Master is grateful.

30:17: This is glorification from Him, the Most High, to His Holy Self, and guidance to His servants to glorify and praise Him at these successive times that indicate the perfection of His power and the greatness of His authority, in the evening, which is the approach of the night with its darkness, and in the morning, which is the dawning of the day with its light. And the verses about this are many. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Zaban bin Fa’id told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Mu’adh bin Anas Al-Juhani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham His faithful friend? Thus do We bring forth the dead that you may remember. And for this reason He said here, And thus you will be brought forth.

30:20: God Almighty says: And among His signs indicating His greatness and perfect power, is that He created your father Adam from dust then, behold, you are human beings dispersing Your origin is from dust, then from despised water, then He took form and became a clot, then a lump of flesh, then it became bones, its shape in the shape of a human being, then God clothed those bones with flesh, then He breathed into him the soul and behold, he was all-hearing and all-seeing. Then, as his life grew longer, his strength and movements became more perfected until he built cities and fortresses, traveled to the ends of the regions, rode the seas, and traversed the ends of the earth, earning and gathering wealth. He had thought, insight, cunning, deceit, opinion, knowledge, and breadth in the affairs of this world and the hereafter, each according to his ability. So glory be to He who empowered them, directed them, subjugated them, and directed them to various forms of livelihood and earnings, and differentiated between them in knowledge and thought, beauty and ugliness, wealth and poverty, and happiness. And misery, and that is why God Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly, you were human beings dispersing. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed and Ghandar told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Qasama bin Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created Adam from a handful which He took from all of the earth. Then the children of Adam came according to the proportions of the earth. Among them came the white, the red, the black, and those in between, the wicked, the good, the easy, the rough, and in between.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Aouf al-A’rab. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith. Rather, there would have been aversion if the mates were from a different kind. A man keeps a woman only because of his love for her or mercy for her, such that she will have a child from him, or because she needs him for support, or for the sake of intimacy between them, etc. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.

30:33: God the Almighty says, informing us about people that when they are forced to call upon God alone, with no partner, and that when He bestows blessings upon them, a group of them, when they have the choice, associate others with God and worship others besides Him. God the Almighty says, That they may disbelieve in what We have given them, with some people using the lam of consequence, and others using the lam of justification, but it is an justification for God's ordaining that for them. Then He threatens them with His saying, Then you will come to know. Some of them said, "By God, if a guard were to threaten me, I would fear him. So how can it be, when the one being threatened here is the one who says to a thing, "Be," and it is? Then He says, denouncing the polytheists for what they invented of worshipping other than Him without proof, argument, or evidence: "Or have We sent down to them an authority, meaning an argument, so it speaks, meaning it utters what they used to associate with Him?" This is a question of denial, meaning they did not have any of that. Then God the Almighty said: "And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice therein; but if evil befalls them for what their hands have put forth, at once they despair. This is a denial of man as such, except for the one whom God protects and guides, because when a person is blessed with a blessing, he becomes arrogant and says, The bad deeds have departed from me. Indeed, he is [truly] joyful and boastful." That is, he rejoices in himself and boasts to others. And if hardship befalls him, he despairs and loses hope that he will ever obtain any good after that. God the Almighty said: "Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds." That is, they are patient in times of hardship and do righteous deeds in times of ease. As it is proven in the Sahih: "Amazing is the believer; God does not decree a decision for him except that it is good for him. If ease befalls him, he is thankful and that is good for him; and if hardship befalls him, he is patient and that is good for him." And God the Almighty said: "Do they not see that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it?" That is, He is the One Who disposes and does that by His wisdom and justice, so He expands for some people and restricts for others. "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe."

30:38: God Almighty says, commanding that the relative be given his due i.e. of kindness and kinship ties, and the needy i.e. the one who has nothing to spend on or has something that is not sufficient for him, and the wayfarer i.e. the traveler who is in need of provisions and what he needs for his journey, that is best for those who desire the countenance of God i.e. to see Him on the Day of Resurrection, which is the ultimate goal, and those are the successful i.e. in this world and the hereafter. Then God the Almighty said: And whatever you give in interest to increase within the people’s wealth does not increase with God. That is, whoever gives a gift intending that people will return to him more than what he gave them, then there is no reward for him from God. This is how Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and Ash-Sha’bi interpreted it. This action is permissible even though there is no reward for it, except that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) specifically forbade it, as Ad-Dahhak said. He provided evidence for this by his statement: And do not bestow a favor expecting more in return. That is, do not give a gift intending more in return. Ibn Abbas said: “Usury is of two types: Usury that is invalid, meaning usury of sale? And usury that is permissible, which is a man’s gift that he wants to receive multiples of. Then he recited this verse: “And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people’s wealth - it does not increase with God.” Rather, the reward with God is in zakat, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God - those will receive doubled. That is, for whom God will multiply the reward and recompense. As it came in the Sahih: “And no one gives in charity the equivalent of a date from lawful earnings but that the Most Merciful takes it in His right hand and makes it grow for its owner, just as one of you makes his foal or young camel grow, until the date becomes greater than a mountain.” God the Almighty said: God is He who created you and then provided for you meaning He is the Creator, the Provider. Man emerges from his mother's womb naked, with no knowledge, hearing, sight or strength, then He provides him with all of that after that, as well as feathers, clothing, money, property and earnings. As Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Salam Abu Shurahbil, on the authority of Hubbah and Sawa' bin Khalid, they said: We entered upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was fixing something, so we helped him, and he said, Do not despair of provision as long as your heads are shaking, for man is born red with no scale on him, then God the Almighty provides for him. And the Almighty’s saying: Then He causes you to die meaning after this life, Then He brings you to life meaning on the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: Is there any of your associates meaning those you worship besides God who does any of that? meaning none of them is able to do any of that. Rather, God, the Exalted, the Majestic, is the One who is independent in creation, provision, life, and death. Then He will resurrect the creation on the Day of Resurrection. That is why He said after all of this: Glory be to Him and far above what they associate with Him. Meaning, He is exalted, sanctified, transcendent, glorious, and mighty above having a partner, peer, equal, son, or parent. Rather, He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.

30:52: God Almighty says: Just as you are not able to make the dead hear in their graves, nor convey your words to the deaf who do not hear and who nevertheless turn away from you, likewise you are not able to guide the blind to the truth and turn them back from their misguidance. Rather, that is up to God, for by His power He makes the dead hear the voices of the living if He wills, and He guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and that is not for anyone other than Him. For this reason, God Almighty said: You only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims, meaning submissive, responsive, and obedient. Those are the ones who hear the truth and follow it, and this is the state of the believers, while the first is like the disbelievers, as God Almighty said: Only those who hear respond, and the dead - God will raise them up, then to Him they will be returned. The Mother of the Believers, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used this verse, You do not make the dead hear, as evidence for the delusion of Abdullah ibn Umar in his narration of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressing the dead who were thrown into the well of Badr after three days, and his rebuking and reprimanding them. Until Omar said: O Messenger of God, why are you addressing people who have become corpses? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you do not hear what I say more than they do, but they do not respond. Aisha interpreted it as meaning that he said: They now know that what I used to say to them was the truth. Qatada said: God brought them back to life for him so that they could hear his words as a rebuke, rebuke, and vengeance. The most correct narration according to scholars is that of Abdullah ibn Umar, as it has many evidences to support its authenticity. The most famous of these is what Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: There is no one who passes by the grave of his Muslim brother whom he knew in this world and greets him, except that God restores his soul to him so that he may return the greeting.

30:54: God the Almighty points out that man moves through the stages of creation, one state after another. His origin is from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh, then he becomes bones, then the bones are covered with flesh, and the soul is breathed into him. Then he emerges from his mother's womb weak, thin, and feeble. Then he grows up little by little until he is a child, then a youth, then a young adolescent. This is strength after weakness. Then he begins to decrease, so he matures, then becomes old, then becomes decrepit. This is weakness after strength. So his will, movement, and power weaken, his body turns gray, and his outward and inward characteristics change. For this reason God the Almighty said: "Then, after strength, He made weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills." That is, He does what He wills and disposes of His servants as He wishes. And He is the Knowing, the Competent. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us from Fudayl and Yazid, Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us from Atiyyah al-`Awfi who said: I recited to Ibn `Umar, God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness. So he said, God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness. Then he said: I recited to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as I recited to him, and he took from me as I took from you. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it and authenticated it from the hadith of Fudayl. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Jabir from Atiyyah from Abu Sa`id in a similar manner.
30:55: God Almighty tells us about the ignorance of the infidels in this world and the hereafter. In this world, they worshipped idols, and in the hereafter, they will also be extremely ignorant. One example of this is their swearing by God that they had only remained in this world for one hour. What they meant by that was that no proof would be established against them and that they would not be given respite so that they could be excused. God the Almighty said: “Thus they used to lie. And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, ‘You have indeed remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.’” That is, the believing scholars will respond to them in the Hereafter, just as they established God’s proof against them in this world. They will say to them when they swear that they had not remained more than an hour, You have indeed remained in the Book of God, that is, in the Book of deeds, until the Day of Resurrection, that is, from the day you were created until you were resurrected, but you did not know. God the Almighty said: So on that Day, that is, the Day of Resurrection, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong, that is, their apology for what they did, nor will they be asked to repent, that is, they will not be returned to this world, as God the Almighty said: And if they ask to repent, they will not be among those who are asked to repent.

30:58: God the Almighty says: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example. That is, We have made clear to them the truth, and explained it to them, and presented to them in it examples so that they may understand the truth and follow it. And if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘You are not but falsifiers.’ That is, if they saw any sign, whether it was suggested by them or otherwise, they would not believe in it and would believe that it was magic and falsehood, as they said about the splitting of the moon and the like. God the Almighty also said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign came to them until they see the painful punishment. That is why He said here: “Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of those who do not know. So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth.” That is, be patient in their opposition and stubbornness, for God the Almighty will fulfill what He promised you of His victory over them and making it the outcome for you and for those who follow you in this world and the hereafter. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient. That is, rather, remain steadfast in what God has sent you with. Indeed, it is the truth about which there is no doubt, and there is no deviation from it, and there is no guidance to be followed besides it. Rather, the whole of truth is confined to it. Sa`id said on the authority of Qatadah: A man from the Khawarij called out to Ali may God be pleased with him while he was in the dawn prayer, and said: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate [anything] with God, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers. Ali listened attentively until he understood what he said, then he answered him while he was praying: “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty impress you.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another chain of transmission, saying: Waki` told us: Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Zar`ah, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, who said: A man from the Khawarij called out to Ali, may God be pleased with him, while he was praying the dawn prayer, and said: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate others with God, your work would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, answered him while he was praying: “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty impress you.” Another path Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Al-Ja`d told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Imran bin Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Yahya, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, prayed the dawn prayer, and a man from the Khawarij called out to him, If you associate partners with God, your work will be in vain, and you will surely be among the losers. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.” What was narrated about the virtue of this noble Surah and the desirability of reciting it at dawn Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, I heard Shabib Abu Ruh narrating from a man from among the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led them in the dawn prayer and recited Surat al-Rum in it, which confused them, so he said, "The Qur'an confuses us. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, answered him while he was praying, “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And do not let those who have no certainty make you impatient.” What was narrated about the virtue of this noble Surah and the desirability of reciting it at dawn Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, I heard Shabib Abu Ruh narrating from a man from among the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led them in the dawn prayer and recited Surat al-Rum in it, which confused them, so he said, "The Qur'an confuses us. Some of you pray with us but do not perform ablution well. Whoever attends the prayer with us should perform ablution well." This is a good chain of transmission and a good text, and it contains a wondrous secret and a strange story, which is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was affected by the deficiency in the ablution of the one who followed him. This indicates that the prayer of the follower is connected to the prayer of the imam. End of the interpretation of Surat al-Rum. All praise and thanks are due to God.
